question: The main road haulage organisations in Italy have sounded the alarm about the intermittent closure, until 2050, of one of the most important gateways from the country’s north-west to France and northern Europe.

The EU was established to provide a single market and equal opportunities among Member States; however, Italy is hemmed in by the Alps and its access to that market is therefore restricted, disrupting business for freight and export entrepreneurs, who have been hit by years of logistical isolation.
The periodic closures are expected to cause the loss of billions of euros and prompt a significant drop in regional and national GDP, particularly in the north-west. In the light of the above: 1.

Is the Commission aware that some 40 000 lorries per month following the Mont Blanc route will return via the Fréjus route, causing congestion along the Turin node and repercussions with regard to costs, emissions and logistics efficiency?
Is it prepared to support the drilling of a second tube through Mont Blanc for the purpose of traffic safety, and how long might that take?

To protect the needs of European exporters and prevent costs being borne by businesses and consumers, exerting a drag on national GDP, is the Commission prepared to support the revision of the protocol to the Alpine Convention?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.11.2025) 1. Maintenance and structural works are needed in particular to ensure the road safety of the infrastructure and to prolong its useful lifetime.

They will therefore have a positive effect for the single market in the long term, even if they require temporary closures and shifting of the traffic on alternative routes in the short term, with the associated consequences mentioned by the Honourable Member. 2.

The Commission is fully engaged in the construction of the Mont Cenis railway tunnel situated on the trans-European transport (TEN-T) core network between Lyon and Turin. It will be opened in 2033 and will allow for a modal shift towards railways alleviating the road traffic via available road tunnels of Fréjus and Mont Blanc. 3.

Article 11 of the Transport Protocol to the Alpine Convention1, to which the Honourable Member refers, limits the construction of new, large-capacity roads for transalpine transport. It is not planned to revise this provision which ensures the right balance between transport needs and environmental protection.
